text:
Strata upstream sync skill v1 — synthetic forward evaluation

Scope and limits

This is a read-only behavioral evaluation of the supplied synthetic fixture. It does not establish hardware performance, correctness on real inputs, successful integration, or current upstream revisions. No fetching, Git mutation, build, test, GPU, service, external action, or cleanup was performed. The fixture gives no upstream/fork source SHAs, source diffs, binary/compiler/driver details, model identity, or deployment test results, so no revision-level integration decision can be final.

Concrete execution plan if the run is authorized and the upstreams are available

1. Start from the current Strata work instructions and artifact retention policy. Read the latest committed evaluation reports and registry; locate canonical Niko1221/Strata, MistVVK/XeStrata, and this fork without changing the existing checkout. Record remotes, worktree/branch state, starting fork revision, each upstream revision, and current accepted component revisions. Do not infer that the two upstreams are identical.
2. Pin target SHAs for both upstreams. Compare commit ranges, endpoint trees, and dependency changes. Build a feature inventory by user-visible capability and a component inventory by inference path. Deduplicate shared-origin changes while preserving provenance. Trace functionality placed in C++ generate as well as server/UI/setup files.
3. For every feature, record mandatory status, dependencies, intended fork location, behavior contract, matching existing behavior (with tests/evidence), and status. Separate required bug/API behavior from optional speed work. Keep unsupported or unadaptable items as explicit blocked/held entries with reasons.
4. Build and run each unmodified upstream separately on the Intel SYCL GPU plus AVX2 CPU. Establish whether each actually supports this environment before drawing performance conclusions. Keep the upstream bench.sh and standard client unchanged; use the same client SHA and long input for each endpoint. First inspect the real help and project procedure. Record all argv/effective settings and at least three individually timed alternating runs. Measure startup/load, prefill, decode, and whole-request time separately. Then perform bounded parameter searches (chunk, memory/cache allocation, worker/task settings, relevant backend and speculative decoding) and report the explored range and the best setting for each phase. Preserve box-default and tuned results separately.
5. For every inference candidate, verify the actual model path, quantization, tensor shapes, device capability, token count, prefill/decode role, precision and synchronization/lifetime behavior. Use identical fixed history and state for correctness comparisons. Record component timing and an isolated candidate model comparison against the current best fork config. Keep dispatch limited to confirmed shapes/capabilities; retain validated fallback elsewhere.
6. Integrate mandatory feature behavior and only the inference components justified by evidence. Run functionality checks separately from numerical, fault/recovery, long-input and performance validation. Compare post-integration results against the same current-best fork baseline, including earlier faster configurations; investigate prefill and decode independently. Confirm physical context use and RESTORE behavior before claiming 262144-token completion.
7. Save source/revisions, commands, environment, individual results, correctness/fault evidence, feature/component tables, decisions, unresolved questions, and retention manifest according to repo policy. The allowed user authorization determines whether commit/push is in scope; a skill instruction alone must not imply external publication authority.

Fixture-based feature decisions

| Item | Decision now | Reason / evidence still needed |
|---|---|---|
| api-stream-recovery (server/API and C++ generate) | Mandatory feature; plan adaptation, integration pending | Requires new engine error/status interface. Preserve error/status semantics and recovery contract in this fork. Need upstream interface/source diff, error cases, streaming/cancel/recovery behavior, and server plus C++ generate tests. No integration is demonstrated. |
| cli-chat-mode | Mandatory CLI functionality; plan integration, pending | Old fork has no equivalent. Need option/help/default behavior and interaction with API/config verified from diff and CLI tests. |
| iq3-gu-gpu prefill | Upstream candidate only; do not mark adopted | Matched synthetic runs: fork 50,49,51 us (median 50); upstream 40,41,39 us (median 40), fixed-input finite checks pass. A promising ~20% component timing advantage, but lacks real source/capability parity, full numerical/state checks, physical model workload and model-level impact. Must confirm it is the Intel SYCL path and representative IQ3 GU shapes, then compare bounded isolated and model runs. |
| iq3-down-gpu prefill | Keep fork implementation as current choice | Matched synthetic runs: fork median 80 us; upstream median 110 us; correctness passes. Candidate is materially slower on this fixture. Need verify matched shapes/device/compiler and ensure no required correctness fix is embedded in upstream change. |
| iq3-cpu-nt1 decode | Keep fork implementation as current choice | Matched synthetic runs: fork median 3 us; upstream median 5 us; correctness passes. Confirm AVX2 flags and decode workload parity; no evidence supports replacement. |
| iq3-cpu-nt8 | Upstream candidate, dispatch only if later validated; otherwise keep fork fallback | Matched synthetic runs: fork median 10 us; upstream median 4 us; correctness passes. This is a distinct multi-token CPU role and cannot be generalized to NT1. Need ensure NT8 is exercised in the model, source/capability and flag parity, numerical/state checks, and isolated model comparison. |
| Other inference parts / formats / roles | Not evaluated | Fixture contains no evidence for other quantizations, Attention/GDN, projections, transfer, scheduler, layouts, GPU NT variants, etc. They remain explicit inventory tasks after full diff review. |

Whole-engine / performance decisions

The upstream default result (400 prefill t/s, 9 decode t/s, chunk 512, MTP off) is below the fork's recorded best (646/14, chunk 8192, MTP on), but settings differ and upstream parameter search was not performed. It does not justify rejecting upstream parts or replacing the engine. The whole-model partial candidate is unmeasured. Run tuned upstream and candidate component configurations with the unchanged upstream bench.sh and standard client; then compare partial integration to fork best under equivalent settings. Report separate prefill/decode results, not a blended score.

The fixture says the upstream bench long case used 32049 input tokens and 24 output tokens. Report it as 32049, not 32768. A 24-token decode is short and cannot settle long-decode behavior. It also notes an earlier generation-128 result, a current generation-24 result, and source changed between them; these are not a valid before/after comparison without matching source and workload. Preserve each result's identity, rerun equivalent cases, and add a longer decode case if decode behavior is in scope.

Maximum context decision

262144 is only configured. Largest physical test is 65536, so maximum-context completion is unverified. Do not claim 256K support as validated. Required evidence includes a physical input that reaches the intended context boundary while preserving output room, final-cell/boundary cases, capacity/state checks, and relevant RESTORE/continuation checks. Report exact physical input/output lengths and whether the full context was actually consumed. The 32049-token bench case and 65536-token test do not establish 262144-token completion.

What can and cannot be concluded from this fixture

Can conclude: API recovery and CLI chat mode are mandatory feature gaps to address; among the four measured synthetic components, GU GPU and CPU NT8 merit focused evaluation, while the fork's Down GPU and CPU NT1 are the present choices. The default whole-engine comparison is confounded by settings, and maximum context is unverified.

Cannot conclude: actual performance or correctness on the target machine; any real feature has been implemented; any kernel has been integrated; tuned upstream performance; model-level benefit or regression; full context completion; complete feature coverage; current upstream revisions; or successful validation. No item is “measured/merged/integrated” by this evaluation.

Skill operational issues found

1. Step 1 and the git-workflow skill prescribe ghq/worktree activity, while step 2 says to fetch, and step 7 says commit/push at boundaries. The skill does not first make these contingent on user scope, the supplied read-only constraint, artifact retention policy, dirty-tree state, or publication authorization. A literal run can violate explicit task limits or publish results. The skill should state that workflow mutations and network actions are subordinate to the active request and only occur when authorized.
2. The blanket rule “all non-inference features must be integrated” can force unsuitable, insecure, incompatible, or unsupported behavior into a fork. It needs an exception/status path for incompatibility, security, user constraints, and missing dependency/validation evidence; “mandatory” should describe evaluation, not guarantee shipping.
3. The required multi-agent instruction fixes models and asks Main to avoid intervening, even when those models/delegation are unavailable or inappropriate, and does not account for task limits forbidding delegation. The later caveat partly acknowledges environment mismatch but still leaves delegation as a default. Make delegation optional and subordinate to user instructions, with single-agent completion allowed.
4. The bench instructions assume an upstream bench.sh and compatible server/client. They say to inspect help, but do not define a fallback or an explicit “not runnable / not comparable” result when a project lacks the script, target backend, or a compatible API. Avoid silently substituting a different benchmark.
5. “At least three” runs is useful, but there is no stop rule for unstable/failing workloads or resource safety bounds for tuning. Require bounded searches, preserve failed/partial outcomes, and stop before risky or destructive operations; the GPU section covers some risks but not general tuning.
6. The 256K section is strong on physical evidence, but “input ... uses 262144 and has no output room” should be operationalized with exact token accounting and a separate near-boundary case that leaves output room. Otherwise a test can satisfy either condition ambiguously.
7. Artifact retention asks for all individual results and recommends committing/pushing while the host AGENTS policy requires deleting successful oversized traces and retaining compact evidence. Clarify that report completeness means durable compact samples/metadata, not indiscriminate raw-trace retention.
